summary: The study demonstrates the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of Ga2O3 films using Ga2(NMe2)6 as the gallium precursor and water as the oxygen source. The process operates within a temperature range of 170 to 250 °C, achieving a growth rate of 1.0 Å/cycle. The films are amorphous upon deposition but crystallize to α-Ga2O3 upon annealing between 700 and 900 °C under nitrogen. The ALD process provides low growth temperatures, surface-saturative growth, and a wide ALD window, resulting in high-quality Ga2O3 films with low impurity levels.
evidence: The atomic layer deposition growth of Ga2O3 films was demonstrated using Ga2(NMe2)6 and water with substrate temperatures between 150 and 300 °C. At 250 °C, surface saturative growth was achieved with Ga2(NMe2)6 vapor pulse lengths of ≥1.5 s. The growth rate was 1.0 Å/cycle at substrate temperatures between 170 and 250 °C. The as-deposited films were amorphous, but crystallized to α-Ga2O3 films upon annealing between 700 and 900 °C under a nitrogen atmosphere.
